verses.1: My son, if you accept my words and store my commandments within you,
verses.2: incline your ear to wisdom, let your heart be attentive to understanding,
verses.3: for if you call out for discernment and raise your voice for understanding,
verses.4: you must seek it as silver and search for it as hidden treasure.
verses.5: Then you will understand the fear of the LORD and find the knowledge of God.
verses.6: For the LORD grants wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
verses.7: He stores up success for the upright, and is a shield to those who walk blamelessly,
verses.8: guarding the paths of justice and preserving the way of his faithful ones.
verses.9: Then you will understand what is right, judgment, and every good path.
verses.10: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will bring delight to your soul,
verses.11: wisdom will guard you and understanding will watch over you,
verses.12: to rescue you from the way of the wicked, from the man who speaks deceptively,
verses.13: from those who abandon the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
verses.14: those who rejoice in doing evil and celebrate in deceit,
verses.15: whose ways are crooked and whose paths are devious,
verses.16: to keep you from the straight path, to lead you into a foreign way.
verses.17: The woman who abandons the teaching of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God,
verses.18: for her house is set toward death, and her paths lead to the world of the dead,
verses.19: none who go into her will return, nor will they grasp the paths of life.
verses.20: So that you may walk in the good ways and keep the paths of the righteous,
verses.21: for the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it,
verses.22: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous will be torn from it.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "knowledge will bring delight to your soul" — "knowledge will bring grace to your throat" is an alternate rendering of נפש here, but the context supports a more holistic interpretation of "soul" as a person's inner being.
- v. 16: "lead you into a foreign way" — the Hebrew term נכרית could also be rendered as "strange" or "alien," but "foreign" fits the semantic field of guidance and direction.
- v. 17: "the woman who abandons..." — the reference is to a metaphorical "strange woman" or unfaithful partner, common in wisdom literature, and not to be taken as a literal woman.
- v. 18: "the world of the dead" — the Hebrew refers to שְׁאוֹל, commonly rendered as "Sheol," but the context here is metaphorical, so a more accessible rendering is chosen.
